newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Merchants Port plans share rights.
newsitem.headline: China Merchants Port plans share rights.

text.p: China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to make a three-for-10 rights issue for its B shares priced at 4.5 yuan each, paid in Hong Kong dollars.

The port company, which has A and B shares listed in Shenzhen, decided at a recent meeting of shareholders to issue 39.55 million new shares for its 131.84 million B shares, the company said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The statement did not give a conversion rate on Hong Kong dollars for the rights issue price.
Merchants Port, which also has a secondary listing in Singapore, said it would channel proceeds to basic port facilities and debts.
The statement said the company planned to implement the new rights offer within six months.

"The pricing of the B rights offer seems to be about right as the share price has been hovering mostly above HK$5 since January this year," an analyst with Central-South Securities Co told Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"Most of the rights shares are expected be snapped up."

Last July, the company made a three-for-10 rights offer to holders of institutional shares and A shares at 4.5 yuan per share and proceeds are being used to renovate port facilities, build warehouses and repay bank loans.
The company's A shares closed at 13.25 yuan last Friday and its B shares were seen at HK$5.62.
Trading in the shares was suspended on Monday and Tuesday morning due to the rights issue announcement and the convening of a shareholders meeting.
Trading in the company's shares will resume on Tuesday afternoon.

The company earlier reported an unaudited interim post-tax profit for the first half of 1996 of 55.6 million yuan, down eight percent from the same period in 1995. It has yet to post 1996 annual results.
